result.title: Unlocking Spatial Grounding in Flow-Matching Models via SNR Tuning
result.summary: Despite the success of foundation models in image synthesis, achieving fine-grained spatial control remains a significant challenge, typically requiring auxiliary structural adapters or complex inference-time steering. While modern vision-language (VLM) text encoders possess the latent capacity to represent spatial coordinates, generative models often fail to leverage this information. We demonstrate that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distribution is a critical determinant of spatial grounding in flow-matching models. Using a novel synthetic benchmark of geometric primitives, we isolate structural mechanics from textural complexity inherent in natural imagery and introduce a rigorous color-aware layout metric to quantify spatial fidelity. We show that training on a centered SNR distribution results in poor layout adherence (25.9%). Instead, we identify high-noise regimes as a "critical learning phase" for spatial grounding. Shifting the training focus toward these stages increases layout adherence to 80.8%, effectively reaching the 83.6% reconstruction ceiling of the underlying variational autoencoder. We find that the necessity for this shift scales with resolution and aspect ratio variance, and that the conservative noise schedules employed by models like FLUX.1 are insufficient for precise layout adherence. Finally, we show that these findings translate to real-world imagery via the COCO dataset (1.0 vs. 57.3 Average Precision), where state-of-the-art layout adherence is unlocked through distribution tuning alone, without architectural modifications.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在流匹配图像生成模型中考察训练噪声的信噪比（SNR）分布对空间布局控制的影响，构建几何图元合成基准与颜色感知布局指标，发现把训练重心移向高噪声阶段可把布局符合率从 25.9% 提升到 80.8%，并在 COCO 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心线索是「表示里已有空间坐标、但模型未加利用」，且利用与否取决于训练阶段加权，可供核查 LVR 中训练监督分配如何影响视觉/空间 latent 内容是否真正参与输出。
